title: This Number Pays You $4,000 a Month Forever? #Shorts
description:
Invest $1.2 million, take out 4% a year, and you get about $4,000 a month before taxes. But the 4% rule was built to last about 30 years, not forever, and it is not guaranteed: crashes, taxes, fees, and inflation can all shrink it. Reaching $1.2 million takes time more than luck: about $460 a month for 40 years at 7% a year after inflation, which is an assumption, not a promise.

Sources:
[S1] William Bengen, Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data, Journal of Financial Planning (1994), FPA reprint: https://www.financialplanningassociation.org/sites/default/files/2021-04/MAR04%20Determining%20Withdrawal%20Rates%20Using%20Historical%20Data.pdf
[S2] Trinity Study: Cooley, Hubbard & Walz, Sustainable Withdrawal Rates From Your Retirement Portfolio (1999 follow-up to the 1998 study): https://everywhereonce.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/10/trinity-study1.pdf
[S3] Morningstar, The State of Retirement Income: 2025: https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt9415ea4cc4157833/bltb73b87c5d0c70ead/The_State_of_Retirement_Income_2025.pdf
[S4] Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern), Historical Returns on Stocks, Bonds and Bills: https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/histretSP.html
[S5] FRED, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCNS): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCNS

Our own calculation:
[D1] $1,200,000 x 4% = $48,000 a year = $4,000 a month (first year, before taxes and fees).
[D2] $457 a month for 40 years at 7% a year after inflation (monthly compounding) grows to about $1.2 million: $219,444 deposited, about $980,556 from compounding. No taxes, fees, or crashes in the math.
[D3] S&P 500 1928-2025: about 10.0% a year nominal and about 6.8% after inflation, from [S4] and [S5].
